delete.description:
Irreversible, unlike archiving a ticket. Private saved views go with the account - nobody else could see them, and left behind they would be owned by nobody and visible to nobody. Shared views stay with the team, now ownerless. Comments and ticket assignments keep their rows and lose their name: work outlives the people who touched it.

Only your own account. Deleting someone else's would need an authority model this schema does not define.
delete.summary: Delete your own account (this one does delete)

post.description:
Public: this is how a person gets a session. Creates the account and, in the same transaction, its membership of the workspace - creating the workspace first if the install has none. On success it sets the session cookie exactly as login does.

Single-workspace model: when a workspace already exists the new account joins it as a member. There is no invitation or approval step yet (ADR 0004), so until there is, anyone who can reach this endpoint can join - do not expose it beyond a trusted network.

A duplicate email answers 409 `email_taken`. That reveals the address is registered, which a registration endpoint cannot avoid; it costs the same time as a success.
post.summary: Create an account and log in as it

post.description: Seeds three statuses, five starter aspect types and one shared saved view, in the same transaction that creates the team - so a team is never observable half-configured. Everything seeded is an ordinary row: rename it, delete it, replace it. Nothing is privileged, and no default labels are seeded, because a label vocabulary is a team's own.

post.description:
Reads a page. POST rather than GET because nested and/or filters do not encode cleanly in a query string, and a per-caller ticket list is not cacheable - so a GET would buy nothing and cost expressiveness. Nothing is written.

Pagination is keyset: pass the previous page's `next_cursor` back as `cursor`. A cursor is only valid for the filter and sort it was minted under; changing either restarts from the first page.

Filterable and sortable fields:

- `assignee` (uuid)
- `created_at` (time)
- `description` (text)
- `epic` (uuid)
- `label` (uuid_set)
- `project` (uuid)
- `sprint` (uuid_set)
- `status` (uuid)
- `title` (text)
- `updated_at` (time)

Page size defaults to 50 and may not exceed 200.
post.summary: List tickets (a read - see the description for why it is a POST)

delete.summary: Archive a ticket (soft delete - the row and its comments survive)
